newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on trade lull.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on trade lull.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were down at the close after the market ended another day of virtually no trading, dealers said.
The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted May RSS1 buyer at 282.50 cents ($1.13) a kg, down 2.0 cents from Monday. May SMR20 buyer was 1.50 cents lower at 267.50.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 265 cents a kg, SMR CV at 340, SMR L at 320, SMR 5 at 280, SMR 10 at 270 and drum latex FOB at 229.
Traders said there was no buying or inquiries that they knew which could have helped boost prices.

"On the contrary, we had depressing news like the strike at Goodyear," said a trader. About 13,000 members of the United Steelworkers of America walked off their jobs just after midnight on Sunday in the first strike in 21 years at the largest U.S. tyre maker.

The INRO five-day moving indicator was quoted at 217.05 Malaysian/Singaporean cents per kg on April 21, compared to the 218.46 on April 17. The daily indicator was also lower at 214.01 from 216.18 previously.
